timer_tick.meaning: the runtime reprograms PIT channel 0 to 2048 (582.6 Hz) and chains the original 18.2 Hz handler every 32nd tick; note durations are counted in these ticks

beep.meaning: BEEP / BEL character: 800 Hz for 128 timer ticks (4 BIOS ticks)

Gato1.exe.routine_evidence: the routine's dispatch table compares the command letter with 'A'..'G' and its handlers range-check octave (<7), tempo (>=32) and length (<=64): PLAY command parser

play_duration_rule.certainty: standard BASIC PLAY rule; defaults assumed from the BASIC manual, not decoded from the runtime (the runtime stores tempo/length/octave at ds:0x8c/0x8d/0x8b)

morse.source: Gato1.exe, ON v GOSUB dispatcher at file 0xbe4a, branch bodies 0xc1cd-0xc5d4, tone subroutines 0xc5d5-0xc610
morse.verification: all 36 branches decoded; 36 of 36 equal International Morse (A-Z, 0-9)

timing.note: seconds from the standard PLAY rule at default tempo 120 (see play_duration_rule); the runtime's staccato/legato handling (MN/ML/MS) was not decoded, so real tone lengths can be up to 1/8 shorter. The PLAYs are foreground (no MB prefix), so each element blocks the program until finished. There is no extra letter or word gap: characters are sounded back to back, spaces and punctuation are silent.
timing.pitch: no octave command: the runtime default octave 4 applies, note B (about 494 Hz); inferred from the PLAY syntax, the frequency table of the runtime was not extracted

text_to_morse: Subroutine at Gato1 0xbc00-0xbe97 prints one order line (L$, ds:0x2372, read with LINE INPUT #1 from ORDXXn) one character at a time.
v = ASC(LEFT$(L$,1)) - 64 (stored in ds:0x224e): A-Z give 1-26.

If ds:0x2256 < 8 the character is PRINTed; otherwise a FOR 1 TO 340 delay loop runs instead (ds:0x2256 is not identified: it looks like a setting that hides the text so orders must be copied from Morse; inferred, not proved).
L$ is shortened by one character; INKEY$ is polled and any key does SOUND 37,0 and abandons the rest of the orders.

Digits ('0'-'9' give -16..-7) are accepted only when ds:0x9e2 = 1 and become v + 43 = 27..36; letters (1 <= v <= 26) require ds:0x9e2 <> 0; every other character is skipped. ds:0x9e2 is also the duration operand of several SOUND statements, so its role is unresolved (likely a sound on/off setting).
If L$ is now empty the next line is read, so the last character of each line is printed but not sounded.
Otherwise ON v GOSUB (runtime 199b:1def, 36 entries) calls the letter's branch; it GOSUBs the dit/dah subroutines and RETURNs to 0xbe98, which loops to the next character.
Each element subroutine is a single PLAY of one of the four strings; the two-element strings (dit-dah, dah-dit) are used as shortcuts for A, N and adjacent element pairs.
morse.demo_exe: DEMO.EXE contains no PLAY statement and no equivalent dispatcher; its DEMORD text is shown silently (its SOUND calls are effects, not Morse).

unused_play_strings.MBT100L9B: 0xd319, longer blip, background mode; both are sounded in region 64, just before the LOG1 record is written, and are not part of the Morse code
